item.title: Book review: Modern software engineering
item.description: Modern software engineering written by David Farley is a good book to read if you want an overview of a systematic approach to software development that has focus on real delivering real impact instead of where we many times end up planning and focusing on being busy. It is not about throwing away process. It is about a systematic approach (this is engineering) and making use of what makes software different from many other areas, we can create, run, learn from and change the software in minutes. A short summary would be - waterfall is not a good practice in software development, make use of the superpower of short experiments. The book adds on a lot to this, measure, test, characteristics of good software and also some perspectives on the people and organisation that works with the software.

item.title: Book review: The unicorn project
item.description: The Unicorn project is a book about how to (and how not to) develop software in a large company. How do you go from an inefficient, slow and frustrating work environment to a setup where you deliver value fast and people are happy to go to work? Gene Kim’s (the author) answer is DevOps, create teams that understand the business, can work end to end from business need to deployed software and that can do experiments, learn from the deployment and improve.

item.title: Does is matter if I call it a PoC or MVP?
item.description: In software development we run Proof of Concepts (PoCs), do Minimum Viable Products (MVPs), use DevOps and many other activities that have names that are more or less well defined. So when I want to get something done, does it matter what I call it? Yes! Or a longer answer, Yes, it matters in the context where other people interact with your activity, people that finance it, use the output or might fight against it.
